title: Client configuration | Driftwood Python SDK v4
text: Client configuration (Python SDK v4). Pass options to driftwood.Client(...). The timeout_seconds option sets the request timeout for every API call; it defaults to 30 seconds. max_retries defaults to 3 and retries use exponential backoff. base_url overrides the API host. In v4 the old request_timeout option was removed; use timeout_seconds instead.
keywords: python sdk client timeout option default configuration

title: Client configuration | Driftwood Python SDK v3 (legacy)
text: Client configuration (Python SDK v3, legacy). The request_timeout option sets the request timeout in seconds and defaults to 60. retries defaults to 2. This version is no longer maintained; see the v4 documentation.
keywords: python sdk client timeout option default configuration

title: Client configuration | Driftwood Node.js SDK v4
text: Client configuration (Node.js SDK v4). new Driftwood({ timeoutMs }) sets the request timeout in milliseconds; the default is 120000 (120 seconds). maxRetries defaults to 3.
keywords: node sdk client timeout option default configuration

title: driftwood-io/driftwood-python: Official Python SDK for the Driftwood API
text: Official Python SDK for the Driftwood API. Install with pip install driftwood>=4. Quick start: client = driftwood.Client(api_key="...", timeout_seconds=10). See the configuration docs for all client options and their defaults.

title: Driftwood Python client times out after 60 seconds - Stack Overflow
author: devops_dan
text: My Driftwood Python client times out after 60 seconds on large exports. Answer: set request_timeout when creating the client, e.g. Client(request_timeout=300). The default request timeout is 60 seconds.
